The execution flow: (1) compute CRC of the source file, (2) determine the destination directory, (3) if the destination file exists, compute its CRC, (4) if CRCs differ or the file does not exist, attempt to copy the source to destination, (5) if an IOException occurs during copying, the catch block throws a GdxRuntimeException wrapping the IOException, (6) after copying, if the destination file still does not exist, another GdxRuntimeException is thrown. The throw statement `throw new GdxRuntimeException("Error extracting file: " + sourcePath, ex);` occurs specifically when file I/O fails during extraction. This design suggests the programmer intends the exception to be treated as a runtime error, likely expecting callers not to catch it unless necessary. The intent appears to be to simplify the API by avoiding forced checked exception handling for this specific failure, implying the programmer did not expect this runtime exception to be caught by typical callers.
